insights.text: Moderators want a clear head on a weeknight, but they still want to be seen with a cider in hand when friends are round.
Cutting back doesn't mean I want to sit out the weeknight at home with my friends. I just want to drink something different while I'm there.
Moderating is common, with 31% of adults doing it, but only 18% of no/low drinkers would consider this. Being a sensible idea is not yet being a choice.
The audience wants the cider credibility of the parent brand, but a 0.0 that shares the parent's livery is judged as alcohol advertising.
The claim is the grown-up alcohol-free, but the occasion is about belonging with friends. Grown-up could read as abstaining rather than joining in.
The weeknight 0.0 is bought in a shop and opened at home. For most of its sales, the shelf is the first place it is seen and chosen.
Digital takes 58% of spend, but this drink sells mostly off-trade. The online story has to end at the shelf or it ends nowhere.
Cider's season runs May to August, but the 0.0 occasion is the ordinary weeknight at home. It needs a reason to be opened that isn't sunshine.
Same product, two jobs. In Ireland people already know the parent and need reassuring. In GB they have never met it and need introducing.
Ireland's no/low value is growing about twice as fast as GB's. The habit is forming now, so whoever is there first may become the habit.
I'll still have cider on Saturday. This is for Wednesday. The 0.0 sits alongside the weekend drink rather than replacing it.
Three brands hold 71% of volume. What if Lúnasa 0.0 doesn't fight for the weekend round and instead claims the weeknight nobody is speaking to?
What if the 0.0 earned its cider look without the parent's livery, with its own badge that a friend across the table still reads as cider?
Borrow the designated driver move: make the 0.0 a role the table thanks you for, not a restriction you apologise for.
